final.title: The quiet cost of overconfidence in one workflow
final.body:
Overconfidence is usually quiet. It hides in the task you do by memory, so nobody stops to ask whether the process is actually clean, fast, or safe. The cost shows up later as rework, missing approvals, duplicate entries, or a problem that only becomes visible after it has already moved downstream.

For a small business owner, the decision is not “use AI everywhere.” It is simpler: pick one repeatable workflow and check whether you are guessing about its cost. If the task is manual, repeated, and has a visible failure mode, it may be worth testing whether a small automation fits. If it is rare, sensitive, or depends on judgment, manual work may still be the better choice.

Bareni’s diagnostic is built around that kind of decision. The point is to identify one recurring workflow, say honestly whether AI fits, and define scope, measures, and limits before anything is built. Human approval stays in place for money movement and other high-risk decisions. That is not a workaround; it is the control.

A useful first question is plain: which single repeating task do you treat as “fine” without measuring how often it creates rework? Most founders only find the quiet cost after they look for it.
